That economic claim is CORRECTED here: given the observed run-21 data (single pot ~95 USDC vs qualifying cost ~634, the real 6.7x margin), break-even needs the AGGREGATE of pots to exceed ONE qualifying cost (~7 per-token pots at those sizes), not merely two tokens. classificationReport.conservatismNote: CRITICAL RULE 4 (conservative when uncertain) applied to DEDUP-22-001: the default multi-token funding config does NOT breach the 6.7x per-token margin, so the honest baseline severity is Low; Medium materializes only under a specific owner over-funding config. classifiedFindings.label: L-01

classification.assetImpact: Owner-funded nudge-reward tokens (real ERC20 value). story-025's whole-whitelist payout pays the qualifying recipient the PRIOR-accumulated pot of EVERY whitelisted nudge token in one event (_payRewards(recipient, snapshot), line 434), for a SINGLE qualifying cost (mint nudgeSize NFTs). Aggregation amortizes that one qualifying cost across N pots — the economic delta the per-token disposition never weighed.
attackPath: 1. Owner whitelists N nudge tokens and funds each pot individually below the per-token snipe margin (per the 858e9e80 disposition, per-token safety = pot_i well under the qualifying cost; the observed run-21 point was pot ~95 USDC vs qualifying cost ~634, a 6.7x margin).
2. Because the qualifying cost is paid ONCE but ALL pots are swept, per-token safety does NOT compose: break-even shifts from 'each pot < qualifying cost' to 'SUM(pot_i) < qualifying cost'.

3. If the owner funds the whitelist such that SUM(pot_i) exceeds one qualifying cost (at the observed sizes, ~7 per-token pots; fewer if pots are larger), a searcher pays nudgeSize*mintPrice once, front-runs/qualifies, and sweeps the aggregate — net-positive even though the minted NFTs carry no redemption value.

4. The worthless-NFT sunk-cost defense that made the per-token snipe net-negative does not de-fang the aggregate: profit is denominated in the swept reward tokens, and only one mint cost is incurred for N pots.
classification.likelihood: low by default, conditional. No attacker privilege and a standard mempool front-run — BUT profitability requires the owner to fund the whitelist-AGGREGATE past one qualifying cost. At the observed pot/cost sizes that needs ~7 tokens each near the per-token-safe level, or correspondingly fewer larger pots. Ordinary/conservative multi-token funding (a few modest pots) stays within the 6.7x margin and remains net-negative. The owner controls the only precondition; no unprivileged path forces the breach.
classification.assumptions: NFTs have NO redemption value on this project (sunk cost) — holds, and is exactly why per-token was safe. Qualifying cost is a single fixed cost independent of token count. Reward tokens carry real value (they are the incentive).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner funding configuration: SUM of all whitelisted nudge pots exceeds nudgeSize*mintPrice net of the (searcher-discounted) NFT value. Attacker-uncontrollable. Non-malicious owner assumed — this is a NON-OBVIOUS Law-3 footgun: the safe funding threshold silently migrates from per-token to whitelist-aggregate, and an owner reasoning per-token (as the prior triage did) would be surprised.

severityDecision.why: The specific factors that de-fanged the per-token High (worthless NFT + cost-floor) genuinely fail to COMPOSE across tokens, so the aggregate case is a real value-leak path — that is why it is surfaced and not folded under the 858e9e80 wont-fix. But it is filed Low, not Medium, because (a) the default/conservative funding config does not breach the 6.7x margin — the leak needs an owner over-funding of the whitelist-aggregate (external requirement), and (b) CRITICAL RULE 4 mandates the lower classification under genuine uncertainty, and (c) there is no unprivileged theft absent that config. The Medium the earlier partial pass assigned rested on an overstated 'N>=2 profitable' claim that ignores the qualifying-cost magnitude; corrected, the profitability threshold is aggregate-sum > qualifying cost, which is config-conditional.
severityDecision.mediumEscalationTrigger: Re-rate to Medium (C4 'value leak with stated assumptions + external requirements') the moment any live/pending deployment funds the whitelist such that SUM(pot_i) approaches or exceeds nudgeSize*mintPrice. This is the AGGREGATE re-expression of the 858e9e80/521c20ad reopen triggers (a)-(e) — evaluate them against the whitelist-aggregate, never per token. Feeds ledger note P5; does NOT override the per-token wont-fixes.
severityDecision.law3: Classified on the impact the non-obvious footgun unlocks, per Law 3 — surfaced with safe-config guidance, not as a malicious-admin vector.

classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Size the WHITELIST-AGGREGATE, not each token, under the qualifying cost: keep SUM(pot_i across all whitelisted tokens) < nudgeSize*mintPrice at all times, OR scale the qualifying cost by the number of tokens paid, OR pay one token per qualifying batch rather than the whole whitelist. Monitor aggregate pot balances against nudgeSize*mintPrice, not per-token balances.
classifiedFindings.justification: Non-obvious cross-token summation footgun; real but config-gated value leak of owner-funded reward tokens, no direct unprivileged theft absent an over-funding config — filed Low with a hard, documented Medium-escalation trigger (aggregate pots > qualifying cost), flagged borderline for human triage.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02

classification.assetImpact: None to protocol funds. minRewards[] is a FLOOR check only — the whole prior pot is paid regardless of the floor — so no over- or under-payment of assets results. Worst case for a caller is an unexpected revert (their token's floor applied to a different token after a swap-and-pop reorder) or a floor guarantee bound to a different token than intended (positional/UI mismatch).
attackPath: 1. Owner removes a whitelisted token via setNudgeTokenWhitelist(token,false); removal is swap-and-pop (the LAST token moves into the removed slot), so getNudgeTokens() ordering changes.
2. A caller who fetched the token order before the reorder submits batchMint with a positional minRewards[] now mapped to the wrong tokens.

3. The per-token floor check compares each stale minRewards[i] against a different token's snapshot — a spurious revert (self-DoS) or a floor silently protecting the wrong token. CODE-VER-07 confirms index integrity + length checks (no OOB, no wrong-token payout).
classification.likelihood: low — requires an owner whitelist mutation to interleave with a caller who did not re-fetch getNudgeTokens() immediately before batchMint. The NatSpec explicitly documents the re-fetch requirement.
classification.assumptions: Caller supplies a positional minRewards[] fetched before an owner reorder and does not re-fetch.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner remove-token operation interleaved with a caller's batch; caller reliance on a stale ordering snapshot.

classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Callers/UI must re-fetch getNudgeTokens() immediately before every batchMint (already in NatSpec). Consider a token-keyed minRewards mapping or an expected-ordering hash argument so positional drift fails closed against the intended token rather than a silently-rebound one.
classifiedFindings.justification: C4 QA/Low: incorrect-state-handling / ordering footgun with floor-only impact and no asset movement (whole pot paid regardless of minRewards, so no value leak). Ceiling Low/QA. Kept distinct from L-05 990d8c37 and Q-01 cabd4a3d per dedup — different root cause, do not collapse.

manualReviewRecommendations.status: MANUAL-REVIEW — severity RECOMMENDATION only, NOT auto-filed
manualReviewRecommendations.possibleClassMatch: Ledger M-02 911c54fd (NFTStaker.emergencyWithdraw survivor over-emission), wont-fix owner-ack 2026-06-09
recommendationRationale: The M-02 MEDIUM-grade impact does NOT inherit on the depletion variant. M-02's over-emission relied on NFTStaker's totalStaked-DEPENDENT rate (a leaver re-rated survivors upward). NFTStakerDepletionV2's emission is budget/window and totalStaked-INDEPENDENT, so an emergency exit does not re-rate survivors (WATCH-17; ECON-VER-01 verified V2 solvent, no over-emission). The impact that justified Medium is absent on V2 — honest severity is Low/QA.

The wont-fix RATIONALE, however, does NOT transfer and must not be silently extended: premise (a) 'deployed + non-upgradeable' is FALSE (V2 undeployed — fix is nearly free); premise (b) 'no migrate-on-behalf' is FALSE (V2 has depositFor/migrator plumbing). Only (c) pullAndRefresh survives. Folding V2 into 911c54fd's wont-fix would be an undisclosed override on a fixable contract (disclose-when-refiling-owner-wontfix).
operatorDecision: (a) Land the cheap settlement fix on the undeployed V2 file (the premises that justified accepting the residual are false here — fixing is nearly free); OR

(b) File a linked Low/QA stub extending disposition to V2 with a V2-SCOPED rewritten rationale (staker-independent rate => benign), explicitly NOT resting on the falsified deployed/no-migrate premises.
Do NOT close as acknowledged (that suppresses live code on a still-patchable contract). Do NOT auto-extend the M-02 Medium wont-fix verbatim. (P7)
manualReviewRecommendations.recommendation: Recommend LOW disposition on the V2 instance: the Medium-grade over-emission mechanism does not survive the totalStaked-independent depletion accounting. Carrying it forward as a Medium would overstate and be rejected downstream. Stays a manual-review item; the call is the operator's.
